grasses.title: Cynodon dactylon
grasses.author: (L.) Pers.
grasses.reproduction: Seeds and vegetative parts (stolons and rhizomes)
grasses.characteristics: Stems are branching, spreading on the ground, and rooting at the nodes; leaves are covered with long white hairs around the ligules; spikes are terminal and finger-like; and seed heads consist of 3 to 7 finger-like spikes measuring 4cm long. C. dactylon can be easily differentiated from Panicum repens and Paspalum distichum through its 2-3 leaves that grow on each node on extended runners.
grasses.impacts: C. dactylon is a C4 weed. It is an alternate host of disease-causing pathogens such as Bipolaris oryzae and Rhizoctonia solani. It can produce up to 230 seeds per panicle.

grasses.title: Dactyloctenium aegyptium
grasses.author: (L.) Beauv.
grasses.reproduction: Primarily by seeds and sometimes by stolons
grasses.characteristics: D. aegyptium has basal stems that are creeping, rooting, and dichotomously branching. Its upper stems bearing the flowers are slightly ascending (erect). Its digitate inflorescence appears like starfish or bird’s foot.
grasses.impacts: D. aegyptium is a C4 plant and i well-adapted to drier areas. A single plant can produce up to 66,000 seeds. It can reduce yield of rice by 10 to 75%. The weed is also an alternate host of tungro viruses and rice bugs.

grasses.title: Digitaria ciliaris
grasses.author: (Retz.) Koel.
grasses.characteristics: A creeping grass that has smooth, flattened stems. Basal parts of the stems are more or less lying on the ground while the upper stems are ascending. It has thin and narrow-lanceolate leaves; prominent, and membranous ligules that are clasping the stem. Inflorescence is composed of 3-6 pseudo-spikes digitally arranged as pseudo-whorls at the apical portion.
grasses.impacts: D. ciliaris is a C4 weed. A single plant can produce an average of 1,700 seeds. It reduces yield of rice by as much as 62%.
grasses.weakness: D. ciliaris is very sensitive to shading.

grasses.title: Echinochloa colona
grasses.author: (L.) Link
grasses.characteristics: Stems usually grow flat on top of the soil surface while the uppermost portions grow in upward position (ascending). Most stems are purple or reddish. Spikelets are ovate to broad ovate, closely crowded in four rows along one side of the branch, nearly sessile, sometimes with awn measuring less than 1mm.
grasses.impacts: E. colona is a C4  weed. One plant can produce 3,000 to 6,000 seeds. Control of this weed by hand weeding is difficult due to close resemblances of its young seedlings to rice at early stages. Its full competition at ratios of 4:1 and 8:1 (weed: rice) reduces yield of rice by 86% and 93%, respectively. The weed can also act as alternate host of other pests such as Sarocladium oryzae causing sheath rot of rice, rice bug, and rice black bug.

grasses.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
grasses.author: (L.) P. Beauv. ssp. hispidula (Retz.) Honda
grasses.description: Antena, bayakibok, biyuro, humay-humay, marapagay, naik, palay-pato, telebisyon
grasses.characteristics: Tall and can grow up to 200cm. It has stout and spongy stems; thick roots; and pinkish to purplish, green, soft, nodding panicle with densely crowded, elliptic, and pointed spikelets. Awns are long (2.5cm) and reddish or purplish in color.
grasses.impacts: E. crus-galli is a C4 weed. It can complete its life cycle within 42 to 64 days after emergence producing an average of 2,000 to 40,000 seeds/plant. Some of its variants growing in direct-seeded rice areas in the Philippines are resistant to chloroacetamide (butachlor) and acetanilide (propanil) groups of herbicides. At its early stage, the weed is difficult to control by handweeding because it resembles rice seedlings. The weed can reduce yield of direct-seeded rice by 18 to 57% when its population is at 10 to 80 plants/m2. It is also an alternate food of rice bug and rice black bug in the absence of rice.

grasses.title: Echinochloa glabrescens
grasses.author: Munro ex Hook. f.
grasses.description: Telebisyon, antena, dawa-dawa, marapagay, paray-paray, humay-humay
grasses.characteristics: Erect and can grow up to 100 cm tall. It has panicles that are usually narrow, pyramidal has numerous spikes and green to purplish spikelets that shed at maturity. Awns, if present, are about 1 cm long.
grasses.impacts: E. glabrescens is highly competitive especially when its seedlings grow with rice seedlings during transplanting or after direct seeding. Mean yield reductions in rice could range from 6-73% when its infestation level is at 5 to 40%, respectively. The weed was also reported as alternate food of rice bug and rice black bug in the absence of rice.

grasses.title: Eleusine indica
grasses.author: (L.) Gaertn.
grasses.description: Bakis-bakisan, bang-angan, bikad-bikad, bila-bila, palagtiki, parangis, paragis, sabung-sabungan, sambali
grasses.characteristics: A smooth, tufted, with prostrate to ascending growth habit. Stems are flat, whitish at the base and pale green towards the upper part, and smooth or with long hairs on the edges. Leaves have sheaths that are flat and moderately hairy at the collar; leaf blades flat, linear-lanceolate, and hairy at the upper surface; ligule membranous; long hairs at the junction of blade and sheaths. Auricles are absent. Inflorescences are digitate with terminal whorls consisting of 3 to 6 spikes.
grasses.impacts: E. indica is a C4 weed that can produce 50,000 seeds/plant (average). Its seeds are easily spread when eaten by animals. Its competitive ability against rice has yet to be reported. It is an alternative host to disease-causing organisms of rice such as Rhizoctonia solani, Pyricularia oryzae, and Sarocladium oryzae that cause sheath blight, blast, and sheath rot, respectively.

grasses.title: Ischaemum rugosum
grasses.author: Salisb.
grasses.description: Ipot-doron, bika-bika, bulo-bulo, gulong-lapas, limba-limba, salsaladay, tinitrigo, trigo-trigohan
grasses.characteristics: Erect and can grow  up to 100cm. It has distinctive, prominent transverse ribs or ridges on the lower glume of the spikelets. Its stems are purplish with long hairs at the nodes. It also has leaves that are flat and wide. Its inflorescence is single when young but splits at maturity into two spike-like racemes.
grasses.impacts: I. rugosum is a C4 weed. One plant can produce an average of 4,000 seeds. Failure to control it could reduce yield of rice by as much as 60%. It can also reduce the quality of rice grains by way of contamination when its seeds are accidentally harvested and mixed with rice.

grasses.title: Leersia hexandra
grasses.author: Sw.
grasses.characteristics: Stems are ascending or sub-erect and rooting at the nodes while leaves are linear-lanceolate, acuminate with tiny backward pointing spines at the back of midribs. Ligules are long, round, and thin. Inflorescences have are slender and sub-erect branches; and oblong spikelets.

grasses.title: Leptochloa chinensis
grasses.author: L.
grasses.reproduction: Primarily by seeds but can also propagate by culm cuttings
grasses.characteristics: Slender, tufted, and can grow up to  120 cm tall. Its leaves are linear, flat, thin, membranous, and sometimes reddish or purplish. Its inflorescence has narrowly ovate panicles consisting of 2-7 spikelets.
grasses.impacts: L. chinensis is a C4 weed and can produce 27,000 seeds per plant. It can reduce yield of rice by as much as 48% when allowed to compete at 16 plants/m2. It is also an alternate host of other rice pests such as the green and zigzag leaf hoppers.

grasses.title: Oryza sativa
grasses.author: L. (weedy rice)
grasses.characteristics: Generally taller and have fewer tillers than rice; most seeds have short to long awns that are white, yellow, or purple; most grains have red pericarp while some are off-white; and mature earlier than cultivated rice. Mature seeds of other variants shatter or fall when touched.
grasses.impacts: it absorbs up more nutrients (Nitrogen) in the soil than cultivated rice. It can reduce yield of cultivated rice by 20 to 90% when it competes at densities of 5 to 40 plants m-2. It can also reduce the quality and price of milled rice when its pigmented grains are mixed during harvest. Its control by chemical and manual methods is very challenging particularly in direct-seeded rice because it has the same morphological and physiological characteristics as cultivated rice.

grasses.title: Panicum repens
grasses.author: L.
grasses.description: Tagik-tagik, buwag-buwag, murag bermuda, maralaya, luy-a-luy-a, sabilau, luya-luyahan
grasses.growsIn: Rainfed lowland ricefields and along bunds of irrigated fields
grasses.characteristics: Stem is erect and rooting at the hairless nodes. Leaves are linear-lanceolate, flat, and slightly hairy. Inflorescence has open panicle, slender and erect branches, oval to elliptic spikelets, and slender stalks.

grasses.title: Paspalum conjugatum
grasses.author: Berg.
grasses.description: Kauat-kauat, lakatan, maligoy, pad-pad, kolokawayan, bantotan, kulape, laau-laau
grasses.characteristics: Stems are long creeping, reddish purple, have flattened runners, and hairy nodes. Leaves are flat, linear-lanceolate, hairy at the blades and sheaths. Leaf sheaths are flat, membranous, and with collar of fine hairs below the blade. Ligules are membranous, truncate, and fringed with ring of hairs at the back. Inflorescences have obtuse spikelets, and two terminal spike-like, slender branches.

grasses.title: Paspalum distichum
grasses.author: L.
grasses.description: Bakbaka, barit, damong-ube, lubid-lubid, malit-kalabaw, ragitnit
grasses.reproduction: Rhizomes and aerial stems (stolons), occasionally by seeds
grasses.characteristics: Long creeping and branching stolons; erect, reddish-stems that grow up to 50 cm tall; inflorescence has two erect, Y-looking racemes; and ligules below leaf sheaths.
grasses.impacts: P. disticum is a C4 weed. It can reduce yield of irrigated rice by 4, 45, and 46% when the rice seedlings are planted at distances of 15 x 15cm, 20 x 20cm, and 25 x 25cm, respectively. When growing with rice, P. disticum is difficult to control by handweeding because the detached stolon fragments regenerate easily; and by chemical method because its stolons may escape the toxicity effect of the herbicide applied.
grasses.weakness: its shoot development is largely reduced when shaded and deeply flooded in the field. Repeated harrowings before final levelling and planting also reduce its growth.

grasses.title: Paspalum scrobiculatum
grasses.author: L.
grasses.characteristics: Stems are smooth, slender, purplish at the base, and not creeping. Leaf blades are flat, linear, and have rough margins; leaf sheaths are dark green, hairy near the blades; and ligules are membranous, brown, and long. Inflorescence usually have 3 to 4 spike-like branches arranged alternately; spikelets are two-ranked, orbicular to ovate, pale when young and reddish-brown when mature; stigmas are purple.

sedges.title: Cyperus compactus
sedges.author: Retz.
sedges.characteristics: Its erect stems  can grow up to 70cm tall. It has spongy leaves  that have the same length as the stem. Its inflorescence is a compound of numerous, big, round, spikes and reddish-brown spikelets.

sedges.title: Cyperus compressus
sedges.author: L.
sedges.characteristics: Stems are smooth, green, and densely tufted. Leaves are shorter than stems while its inflorescence is simple and open. Spikes have 3 to 10 crowded spikelets in digitate cluster, while spikelets are greenish and very flattened in appearance.

sedges.title: Cyperus difformis
sedges.author: L.
sedges.description: Baong-baong, bulo-butones, payong-payong, siraw-siraw, treskantos, tuhog-dalang, ubod-ubod
sedges.characteristics: Can grow as tall as 75 cm. It has stems that are pale green and sharply 3-angled at the top; shorter leaves that the stems; umbellate inflorescence that is simple or compound; and numerous spikelets that are globose.
sedges.impacts: C. difformis is a C3 weed. One plant can produce 50,000 seeds with 60% germination. It can complete its life cycle within 30 days and spreads rapidly to become a dominant weed in a ricefield where moisture level is fluctuating. When left uncontrolled, it can reduce yield of rice by as much as 43%.

sedges.title: Cyperus digitatus
sedges.author: Roxb.
sedges.characteristics: Its stems are triangular, flat leaves, compound inflorescence composed of digitately arranged spikes and yellow spikelets.

sedges.title: Cyperus distans
sedges.author: L. f.
sedges.characteristics: Has erect and smooth stems that are triangular; leaves that are as long as the stems; and umbel-type inflorescence. It also has  spreading, slender, red or reddish-brown spikelets.

sedges.title: Cyperus halpan
sedges.author: L. (`haspan`)
sedges.characteristics: Has slender stems with longitudinal median rib on each side. Inflorescence has numerous, long, slender-shaped primary rays and short secondary rays. Its spikelets  are digitately arranged in clusters.

sedges.title: Cyperus imbricatus
sedges.author: Retz.
sedges.characteristics: Coarse, tufted, and erect. Its stems are triangular; leaves are shorter than the stem; compound umbel green inflorescence when young and brown when mature; and with numerous long spikelets.

sedges.title: Cyperus iria
sedges.author: L.
sedges.characteristics: Its stems are smooth and triangular; linear-lanceolate leaves; umbel-shaped inflorescence; and numerous, spreading, erect spikelets that are yellow to yellow-brown.
sedges.impacts: C. iria is a C4 weed. It can establish quickly in the field soon after rice plants are transplanted or direct-seeded. One plant can produce 3,000 seeds. When not controlled, it can reduce yield of rice by as much as 40%. It can also act as alternate host to other rice pests such as green leafhoppers, and plant pathogenic microorganisms such as Pyricularia oryzae, Rhizoctonia solani, and Sarocladium oryzae causing rice blast, sheath blight, and sheath rot diseases, respectively.

sedges.title: Cyperus rotundus
sedges.author: L.
sedges.characteristics: Erect with smooth unbranched three-sided stem, dark green leaves, and flowers in red-brown spikelets. It has extensive underground parts called the basal bulb, rhizomes, tubers, and roots which permit rapid production of multiple young sprouts in the soil.
sedges.impacts: C. rotundus is a C4 plant and is considered as the world’s worst weed. It is a problem due to its prolific behavior in the soil, persistence in harsh environments, and infestations in many crops. In earlier years, it used to be dominant only in upland rice areas in the Philippines but has adapted and infested irrigated and rainfed lowlands as well. Its full competition with upland rice plants reduces rice yield by 42%. Under flooded conditions, it reduces the yield of transplanted rice by  38% while wet direct-seeded rice by 28%. A study suggested that the weed should be controlled at 14-29 DAT for transplanted rice; 18-26 DAS for wet direct-seeded rice.
sedges.weakness: Its leaves are susceptible to infection by Puccinia philippinensis that causes leaf rust. The bulbs of the weed are susceptible to feeding by Bactra sp. The tubers of the weed cannot germinate if plowed under the soil and flooded at the same time. In addition, its growth can be reduced if flooding in the field is applied as early as 7 days after the wet seeding of rice. Meanwhile, the weed is vulnerable to the toxicity of herbicides such as 2,4-D, MCPA, or bispyribac-sodium.

sedges.title: Fimbristylis dichotoma
sedges.author: (L.) Vahl
sedges.characteristics: It has the same characteristics with F. miliacea except that its spikelets are less in number, bigger, and ovoid.

sedges.title: Fimbristylis miliacea
sedges.author: (L.) Vahl
sedges.description: Bungot-bungot, buntot-pusa, gumi, siraw-siraw, sirisibayas, sumpana-balik
sedges.characteristics: Erect with flattened stems that bear 2-4 unequal bracts that are shorter than the inflorescence. Leaves are linear, flat, soft, and overlapping in two rows. Spikelets are numerous, globose to ovoid in shape, and brown to brown-orange.
sedges.impacts: F. miliacea, a C4 weed, is a prolific seed producer. A single plant can produce more than 40,000 seeds.

sedges.title: Scirpus grossus
sedges.author: L.
sedges.characteristics: Has triangular stem. It has numerous brown spikelets that are ovoid.

sedges.title: Scirpus juncoides
sedges.author: L.
sedges.characteristics: Stems are erect and slender. Leaves degenerate to become sheath-like and cover the base of the stems. Fruits are brown to black when mature and broadly elliptical.

broadleaves.title: Aeschynomene indica
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: Erect and robust, and can grow up to 1m tall. Stems are branching and woody at the base. Leaves are even-pinnately arranged with numerous leaflets that are linear or oblong. Flowers are light yellow. Pods are linear-oblong, straight or curved, and composed of 4-8 joints with ridge-like appearance.

broadleaves.title: Alternanthera sessilis
broadleaves.author: (L.) DC.
broadleaves.characteristics: Has a spreading or prostrate growth in the field. It has leaves that are elliptic-lanceolate to linear-lanceolate in shape. Its flowers are white  and are globose to oblong.

broadleaves.title: Alysicarpus vaginalis
broadleaves.author: (L.) DC.
broadleaves.characteristics: Has ascending-erect growth. Stems are branched, stout, and hairless; leaves are ovoid, usually cordate at the base, round at the tip with spines, hairy at the lower surface; flowers usually red with two basal yellow stripes; and pods are yellowish.

broadleaves.title: Amaranthus spinosus
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Alayon, ayang lalaki, ayantoto, baoan, bayambang, harum, gitingiting, kalitis, kalunai, kuanton, kudiapa, kulitis, taikada, uray
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are branched, pale green, with pairs of slender sharp-pointed spines along the axils of the leaves and branches. Leaves are simple, alternate, ovate to broadly lanceolate, and narrow at the base to a petiole. Inflorescences have spikes that are closely in packed and clusters of small, green flowers.
broadleaves.impacts: A. spinosus is a C4 weed that can produce 117,000 seeds/plant. Its competitive ability against rice has yet to be reported. It is an alternative host of Meloidogyne graminicola, a nematode of rice that causes root galls.

broadleaves.title: Amaranthus viridis
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Alom-alom, ayang babae, halom, kilitis, kalunai, kudiapa, kulitis, uray babae
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are much branched, slender, fleshy and reddish, and have no spines along the axils of the leaves and branches. Leaves are simple, alternate, broadly ovate, and indented with a short bristle. Inflorescence have flowers that are green or greenish white, in axillary clusters, and dense flowered spikes.
broadleaves.impacts: A. viridis is also a C4 weed that can produce 7,000 seeds/plant. The weed is reported as an alternative host of Meloidogyne graminicola, a nematode of rice that causes root galls.

broadleaves.title: Ammannia baccifera
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are erect, branched and brownish; branches are longer near the base of the stem and shorter when near the apex; leaves are elliptical to lanceolate, acute at the tip, and narrow toward the basal part. Flowers in clusters are purplish.
broadleaves.weakness: sensitive to herbicide application particularly 2,4-D and butachlor.

broadleaves.title: Ammannia coccinea
broadleaves.author: Rottb.
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are erect, branched, and glabrous, and can grow up to 50 cm. It has leaves that are opposite and auriculate at base. Flowers form petals that are purplish.
broadleaves.impacts: at a population of more than 100 plants m-2, it can reduce yield of rice by up to 21%.

broadleaves.title: Basilicum polystachyon
broadleaves.author: (L.) Moench
broadleaves.characteristics: Srect and branched weed that grows up to 1 m tall. Its stems are 4-angled while leaves are ovate to oblong-ovate, with toothed margins. Racemes bear dense flowers and can grow 10 cm long. Flowers are lilac or pink.

broadleaves.title: Caperonia palustris
broadleaves.author: (L.) A.St-Hil.
broadleaves.characteristics: Stem is erect, branched, and hairy. Leaves are also hairy, broadly lanceolate, serrated on the margins, and alternately arranged on the stem. The flowers are white while the fruits are three-loculed. Each locule contains one grayish (young) to dark brown (mature) and spherical seed.
broadleaves.impacts: In the Philippines, no scientific evidence had been reported that it could reduce the yield of rice. However, some farmers are complaining that it significantly reduced the quality of their harvested grains as well as the net income via the contamination of the weed’s seeds with the rice grains during harvests. In USA, on the other hand, the weed had been reported to reduce yield of drill-seeded rice by 24-31% at 10 plants/m2.

broadleaves.title: Cardiospermum halicacabum
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Alalayon, bangkolon, lubo-lobohan, parol-parolan, paltu-paltukan, parya-aso, paspalya
broadleaves.characteristics: A climbing herb;   has long stems that are slightly hairy; alternating leaves with slender petioles; leaflets that are biternate, ovate to lanceolate, and serrate at the margins and sometimes lobes. Flowers are white and very small while fruits are lantern-shaped.

broadleaves.title: Cleome rutidosperma
broadleaves.author: DC.
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are green to purple, and angular with thin, firm hairs. Leaves have long petioles; three ovate to oblong-lanceolate and ciliate leaflets; center leaflet that are larger than the other two. Inflorescences have flowers that are solitary at the upper leaves; slender stalks;  and lilac to pink petals. The weed has green, thin, long capsules that split into two valves.

broadleaves.title: Cleome viscosa
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Apoy-apoyan, balabalanoyan, hulaya, kabau, lampotaki, tantandok, sili-silihan
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are green, cylindrical, and with hairs; leaves have long petioles and three, oblong to obovate-oblong leaflets; yellow and solitary flowers. The weed also has green and long capsules that split into two valves.

broadleaves.title: Commelina benghalensis
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: Fleshy stems are  creeping to ascending. Leaves are wide in the center, elliptic-ovate and alternately arranged. Petals of the flowers are three to four, and are blue. Petals have different sizes (two to three are large, while one is small) and are blue.

broadleaves.title: Commelina diffusa
broadleaves.author: Burm. f.
broadleaves.characteristics: Fleshy stems are creeping to ascending, and heavily branched. Leaves are narrow, alternately arranged, lanceolate to broadly lanceolate-shaped, and with stem-clasping sheath. Petals of the flowers are three (two large and 1 small), and are blue.
broadleaves.impacts: yield of drilled-seeded rice planted at 215 to 270 plants/m2 were reduced by 18% when C. diffusa was allowed to compete at 22 plants/m2 all throughout the crop’s growing season. In another study, the grain yield of transplanted and wet direct-seeded rice was reduced by as much as 22 and 34%, respectively.

broadleaves.title: Corchorus aestuans
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: It is an erect plant with woody stem and grows smaller than C. olitorius. It has leaves that are ovate or ovately-oblong, finely and crenately toothed with rounded base. Flowers are yellow; capsules has 6 to 8 wings, elongated, and trifid  beak.

broadleaves.title: Corchorus olitorius
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: It is an erect plant with woody stem. It has leaves that are ovate or ovately-lanceolate, margins serrated, toothed, with clusters of small leaves near the axils. Flowers are yellow and its ten-ribbed capsules are elongated and entirely beaked.

broadleaves.title: Eclipta prostrata
broadleaves.author: (L.) L.
broadleaves.characteristics: A C3 weed; its stems  are fleshy, reddish, hairy, and rooting at the nodes. Leaves are  dark green and oppositely arranged, and are linear-oblong to lanceolate, with distinct toothed margins. Flower heads measuring 1-cm diameter bear small white flowers (florets).

broadleaves.title: Eclipta zippeliana
broadleaves.author: Bl.
broadleaves.characteristics: A C3 weed; has the same morphological characteristics as E. prostrata except that its leaves are light green, oblong-obovate to lanceolate, has margins that are coarsely spinulose-toothed. In addition, stems and leaves are much covered with many hairs.

broadleaves.title: Eichhornia crassipes
broadleaves.author: (Mart.) Solms
broadleaves.characteristics: A floating aquatic weed that has short and rosette-like stems. Leaves are ovate to orbicular, with petioles that are swollen and spongy. Flowers are numerous and are purple.
broadleaves.impacts: this weed restricts irrigation and crop growth causing heavy economical losses in rice paddy fields. It can also transmit pathogens that infect several other crops.

broadleaves.title: Hedyotis biflora
broadleaves.author: (L.) Lam
broadleaves.characteristics: Has erect or spreading growth; leaves that are short-petioled, elliptic-ovate to oblong; branched and slender stems; and inflorescence with 2-8 small flowered umbels.

broadleaves.title: Hedyotis corymbosa
broadleaves.author: (L.) Lam.
broadleaves.characteristics: Has erect or spreading growth; its leaves are linear-oblonceolate to linear-oblong and are gradually narrow to the apex. Stems are branched and slender; inflorescence has 2-8 small flowered umbels.

broadleaves.title: Hedyotis diffusa
broadleaves.author: Willd.
broadleaves.characteristics: Has slender and branching stems; thin, linear to wide linear leaves without or with short petioles. Flowers have white to light purple corolla in four parts.

broadleaves.title: Heliotropium indicum
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Ar-aritos, bahu-baho, buntot-leon, elepante, kambra-kambra, higad-higaran
broadleaves.characteristics: It has erect and branched growth habit. It has stem that is covered with hairs; leaves that are ovate to oblong-ovate with rough surfaces; and flowers that are positioned on one side with lavender to white corolla.

broadleaves.title: Hydrolea zeylanica
broadleaves.author: (L.) Vahl
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are hollow, and usually grow flat on top of the soil surfaces while the uppermost portions grow in upward position (ascending). Leaf blades are lanceolate to ovate, glabrous or pubescent, base acute, margin entire, and apex acute. Petals of the flowers are purple-blue.
broadleaves.impacts: cut stems of H. zeylanica can germinate into new seedlings. Thus, it establishes rapidly in the field, particularly under flooded conditions. When not controlled, the weed can reduce the grain yield by as much as 52% for transplanted rice; 6% for wet direct-seeded rice.

broadleaves.title: Ipomoea aquatica
broadleaves.author: Forsk.
broadleaves.characteristics: An aquatic weed that has slender, smooth, and creeping stems; It spreads on the ground or floats on water. Stems are hollow and rooting at the nodes. Leaves are alternately arranged with morphological variations in shapes. Flowers are funnel-shaped and are white to purple.
broadleaves.impacts: how the weed reduces the yield of rice has yet to be reported; it is an alternate host of golden apple snails in the absence of rice plants.

broadleaves.title: Ipomoea triloba
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Aurora, bangbangau, kamkamote, koskusipa, kupit-kupit, halobagbug, muti-muti
broadleaves.characteristics: It is vine that has slender, twining or crawling stems. Its leaves are broadly ovate, entire or somewhat 3-lobed, acuminate with broadly cordate base. Flowers have pink to purple corolla.

broadleaves.title: Limnocharis flava
broadleaves.author: (L.)
broadleaves.reproduction: Seeds and vegetative  propagules called ramet
broadleaves.characteristics: Has triangular-shaped leaves and stalks. Its leaves are erect, papery, light green, ovate to broad elliptic that measure 6-20 cm long. Its stems are hollow and smooth in surface while its flowers are yellow and three-lobed. Its fruits are spherical.
broadleaves.impacts: L. flava is a very competitive weed especially under flooded conditions. In a field study, it significantly reduced the yield of irrigated-transplanted rice (NSIC Rc 144) by 18, 23, 30, and 48%, respectively when allowed to compete at 10, 20, 25, and 30 plants m-2 all throughout the growing season. Competition at 50 to 60 plants/m2 resulted in yield reduction in rice by 63%.
broadleaves.weakness: the weed is sensitive to drier conditions, hence thorough land preparation and proper water management are crucial practices to effectively manage it.

broadleaves.title: Lindernia antipoda
broadleaves.author: (L.) Alston
broadleaves.characteristics: Has spreading or erect growth. Its stems are slender; and leaves are oblong to oblong-lanceolate, shortly petioled, with tooth-like margins. Its flowers lilac.

broadleaves.title: Lindernia procumbens
broadleaves.author: (Krock.) Philcox
broadleaves.characteristics: It has spreading or erect growth; slender and four-sided stems; and leaves that are elliptic, shortly petioled but without tooth-like margins. Flowers are white to lilac.

broadleaves.title: Ludwigia adscendens
broadleaves.author: (L.) Hara
broadleaves.characteristics: Has stems that  creep on the ground or float. Its stems are also rooting at the nodes with their white spongy pneumatophores arising in clusters. Leaves are oblong, elliptic and can grow up to 8 cm long. Flowers have five petals that are white with yellow at the center.

broadleaves.title: Ludwigia decurrens
broadleaves.author: Walter
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are erect, smooth, and four-winged. Leaves subsessile, lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, and entire in margin. The flowers are yellow, with four big obovate-elliptic petals that are abruptly acute at the apex. Capsules are sharply angled or narrowly winged.
broadleaves.impacts: In the Philippines, no scientific evidence has been reported that it could reduce the yield of rice. However, studies in other countries showed that it could potentially reduce the yield of rice by 33% at 4-8 plants/m2. Other studies also showed that the weed is allelopathic to rice and that it has variants that developed resistance to a specific herbicide.

broadleaves.title: Ludwigia hyssopifolia
broadleaves.author: (G.Don) Exell
broadleaves.characteristics: Erect and branched and can grow up to 60 cm tall. Stems are angled, green to reddish, and woody at the base. Leaves are narrow and lanceolate. Flowers are yellow with four ?diamond-shaped? petals (elliptic) 2-3 cm long. Stems are eight, or more than the number of calyx lobes. Capsules are slender, 4-angled, and reddish.
broadleaves.impacts: a C3 weed of rice across a wide range of cultural types, in both clay-loam and clay soils. Full competition at ratios of 4:1 and 8:1 (weed: rice) can significantly reduce rice yield by 64 and 81%, respectively.
broadleaves.weakness: L. hyssopifolia is susceptible to the chrysomelid beetle, Altica sp. with its larvae and adults feeding voraciously on leaves of the weed.

broadleaves.title: Ludwigia octovalvis
broadleaves.author: (Jacq.) Raven
broadleaves.characteristics: A robust, erect, and branched weed than can grow up to 3 m tall. Stems are ridged and sometimes reddish. Leaves are lanceolate. Flowers are yellow, with four big ovate-shaped petals. Stamens are eight, or more than the number of calyx lobes. Capsules bearing the seeds are bigger in size, 4-angled and reddish.
broadleaves.impacts: L. octovalvis is differentiated from L. hyssopifolia and L. perennis by its big, yellow flowers. Out of 350 weed species in rice worldwide, L. octovalvis is fourth in globalscale importance among broadleaves. It invades a wide range of rice culture systems especially dry-seeded rice.
broadleaves.weakness: susceptible to the chrysomelid beetle, Altica sp., with its larvae and adults feeding voraciously on leaves of the weed.

broadleaves.title: Ludwigia perennis
broadleaves.author: (L.) Raven
broadleaves.characteristics: Erect and branched weed that grows up to 30 cm tall. Stems are irregularly ridged and sometimes reddish. Leaves are narrow and lanceolate. Flowers are yellow with four to five egg-shaped (oblong-elliptic) petals. Stamens have the same number as calyx lobes. Capsules bearing the seeds are 4- angled and are reddish.
broadleaves.weakness: L. perennis is susceptible to the chrysomelid beetle, Altica sp. Its larvae and adults feed voraciously on leaves of the weed.

broadleaves.title: Macroptilium lathyroides
broadleaves.author: (L.) Urb.
broadleaves.characteristics: An erect legume that has branchy and woody stems. Leaves are three (trifoliate) and are ovate to lanceolate. Flowers are red-purple. The weed also has green (young) to brown (mature), long and slender pods that bear seeds.

broadleaves.title: Malachra capitata
broadleaves.author: (L.) L.
broadleaves.description: Anabo, bakembakes, bulbulin, buluhan, bulubuluhan, lapnis, pang-balius, labog-labog, tambaking
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are branched and covered with hairs; leaves obscurely and shallowly lobed, finely toothed, base cordate; flowers have yellow petals.

broadleaves.title: Malachra fasciata
broadleaves.author: Jacq. var lineariloba (Turcz.)
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are branched and covered with yellowish hairs; leaves deeply and palmately cut into 5 narrow lobes; flowers have white petals.

broadleaves.title: Marsilea minuta
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: An aquatic fern with long, slender, and branched rhizomes. Leaves have slender and long stalks bearing four triangular-shaped, quadrifoliate leaflets. Spocarps and short hairs can be found at the base of the petiole.
broadleaves.impacts: persistent and very competitive to rice. When not controlled, it can reduce yield of rice by 70%.

broadleaves.title: Melochia concatenata
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: Stems are erect or spreading, and branched with scattered stellate hairs. It has leaves that are oblong to ovate, long, acute, broad base, and rounded or cordate. Inflorescence are terminal or axillary heads with the flowers somewhat crowded, intermixed with linear bracteoles; petals are obovate, white, sometimes pink or pale purple. Fruits are depressed-globose capsules.

broadleaves.title: Merremia emarginata
broadleaves.author: (Burm. F) Hallier f.
broadleaves.characteristics: A slender, twining, sparsely hairy to glabrescent weed. Stems are reddish and rooting at the nodes; leave are kidney to heart shape, often wider than long, and irregularly toothed. Flowers have yellow corolla, and rounded sepals with few to many white weak hairs.

broadleaves.title: Mimosa diplotricha
broadleaves.author: C. Wright ex Sauvalle
broadleaves.characteristics: M. diplotricha is a spreading shrub that turns woody when mature. It has angular stems that are densely covered by numerous reflexed spines. Leaves are alternate, petioled and bipinnate; pinnae has 4-8 pairs; leaflets oblong-linear in many pairs. Petals of the flowers are pink to purple while pods are liner-oblong.

broadleaves.title: Mimosa pudica
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Bain-bain, hibi-hibi, huya-huya, kipi-kipi, makahiya, makahiyang-babae
broadleaves.characteristics: M. pudica is a branched, low or erect-trailing shrub. It has reddish-brown stems that are covered by less numerous spines. Leaves close when touched, digitately arranged at end of each petiole,  leaflets narrowly oblong. Petals of the flowers are pink to purple while pods are flat, slightly curved, and numerous.

broadleaves.title: Monochoria vaginalis
broadleaves.author: (Burm. f.) C. Presl
broadleaves.characteristics: Afleshy, semi-aquatic, monocotyledon weed that has shiny appearance in the field. Its stems are soft, erect, and rooting at the nodes. Flower stalks are long bearing lilac-blue or violet petals that are arranged in 2-6 groups. Its leaves are heart-shaped and petioles that are  soft and hollow.
broadleaves.impacts: M. vaginalis is a C3 weed. Its trait of discontinuous germination allows it to survive and evade weed control. It reduced yield of rice by 16% when it was allowed to compete within 7 to 40 days at 100 plants/m2. Competition until maturity at the same population level reduced yield by 25%.

broadleaves.title: Murdannia nudiflora
broadleaves.author: (L.) Brenan
broadleaves.characteristics: Has branched and creeping stems. Its leaves are long, narrow, and lanceolate. Its flowers are small and purple. Flower-stolons are long, measuring 3 to 7 cm.

broadleaves.title: Phyllanthus debilis
broadleaves.author: Klein ex Willd.
broadleaves.description: kurukalunggai, malakirum-kirum, ngingihel, sampasampalukan, san pedro, sursampalok, talikod, taltalikod, turutalikod
broadleaves.characteristics: P. debilis is an erect, slender, branched, and glabrous herb. Its leaves are numerous, arranged in vertical ranks, oblong to elliptic-oblong, and shortly petioled. It has anthers that are dehiscing horizontally; distinct pedicelled flowers; and smooth capsules.

broadleaves.title: Phyllanthus urinaria
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Apoy-apoyan, ibaiba-an, lurulaioan, minuhminuh, payog, sursampalok, tabi, takum-takum, talindanon, turutalikod
broadleaves.characteristics: P. urinaria is also an erect, slender, branched, and glabrous herb but is smaller than P. debilis. It also has leaves that are numerous, arranged in vertical ranks, oblong to elliptic-oblong, and shortly petioled but has reddish stem and branches. It has anthers that are dehiscing vertically; flowers that have no pedicels or some shortly pedicelled; and rough capsules.

broadleaves.title: Physalis angulata
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.description: Asisiu, kugut, potokan, sisiu, tutulakak, tino-tino
broadleaves.characteristics: An erect and branched weed. It has ovate to oblong leaves and pale-yellowish flowers. Fruits are oblong to ovoid.

broadleaves.title: Pistia stratiotes
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.reproduction: Seeds and vegetative offshoots connected by stolons
broadleaves.characteristics: A floating weed with yellowish-green leaves that form like cabbage plant. It has short flowers and feathery roots. It also bears small plantlets called offshoots that are connected by stolons.
broadleaves.impacts: Studies showed that young P. stratiotes (spread of petal = 3cm) had a lesser or no effect at all on the grain yield of transplanted rice. However, allowing its mature plants (spread of petals = 10cm) to compete in the same population throughout the crop’s growth reduced the grain yield by 12%.

broadleaves.title: Portulaca oleracea
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: An herb with prostrate or spreading growth. It has stems that are branched, succulent, smooth, and reddish. Its leaves are fleshy, alternately arranged, obtuse, oblong-obovate, sessile, and base cuneate. Flowers are yellow with 5 petals.

broadleaves.title: Salvinia molesta
broadleaves.author: D.S. Mitchell
broadleaves.characteristics: It is a hairy floating weed with branched stems. Young leaves are flat and oblong to oval while mature leaves are cordate and slightly folded upward. Leaves are also covered with spine-like hairs. S. molesta usually proliferates to form wide mats. Each node of the slender stem produces three leaves (two are green and floating, and one is brown, root-like, and submerged).
broadleaves.impacts: can reduce yield of rice by 12.5%. Spread of this weed in ricefields was due to mistaken identity as azolla plant.

broadleaves.title: Sphaeranthus africanus
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: An erect weed with stems and branches that have broadly winged leaves. Leaves are obovate to oblong, with wide margins that are finely toothed. It has many round-shaped heads that bear clusters of greenish-white flowers.

broadleaves.title: Sphenoclea zeylanica
broadleaves.author: Gaertn.
broadleaves.characteristics: An erect and branched weed with soft and hollow stems. Leaves are oblong to lanceolate, narrow, and pointed at the tips with short stalks. It has green and cylindrical inflorescence, and white to greenish flowers.
broadleaves.impacts: can reduce yield of rice by 45%. Some variants of the weed have also been reported resistant to 2,4-D.
broadleaves.weakness: susceptible to infection by Alternaria alternata (Fr.) Keissler f.sp. sphenocleae. S. zeylanica inoculated with 10 spores/ml of the fungus showed blighting and wilting after 24 hours of inoculation. At 6 days after inoculation, all S. zeylanica plants died due to severe infection.

broadleaves.title: Trianthema portulacastrum
broadleaves.author: L.
broadleaves.characteristics: It is a succulent and prostrate herb that flat, fleshy, and green or purplish stems. Its leaves are opposite in unequal pairs, ovate to almost round, glabrous, with slightly wavy margins. Flowers usually are white or pale pink to purple.
